summary: ukraine69 harvests Hotaru/goygram session vaults and destroys Telegram accounts at import
details: ukraine69 presents itself as a Ukrainian locale/date helper, but on import it enumerates.vault files across $HOME, HOTARU_* env hints, ~/.hotaru, ~/.local/share/hotaru, /run/hotaru*, /tmp/hotaru*, and cwd ancestors, and reads them via goygram.security._read_vault to extract Telegram session material (auth_key, api_id/hash, server_salt, 2FA password). For each recovered vault, it spawns a detached, isolated Python child that initializes the Telegram TL schema and issues account.deleteAccount against hardcoded Telegram DC IPs (149.154.175.53, 149.154.167.51, 149.154.175.100, 149.154.167.91, 91.108.56.130), including an SRP auth.checkPassword flow when a 2FA password is present, destroying the victim's Telegram accounts from the installer's host using the installer's own stolen credentials. It also establishes persistence by locating the installer's hotaru/__main__.py, writing a backup, and injecting a hook after apply_vault_key_env() that re-runs the schema-load / deleteAccount / vault-unlink chain on every future Hotaru startup. A delayed self-destruct recursively deletes the ukraine69 distribution from ~/.cache/hotaru/module-deps, ~/.cache/pip/wheels, ~/.cache/pip/http-v2, ~/.cache/uv, $TMPDIR/probe-*, and every candidate site-packages directory, purging __pycache__ and.dist-info entries, with a second sweep 30s later to re-wipe reinstalls. A diagnostic marker at $TMPDIR/.u69-agent.log is deliberately kept outside the GC path and records per-stage progress (schema_init_error, schema_ok, goygram_connected, dc=<n>).
